# CountGfxModes <img class="product" src="media/bb-20x14.png" alt="BlitzBasic" title="BlitzBasic" width="20" height="14"> <img class="product" src="media/bp-20x14.png" alt="BlitzPlus" title="BlitzPlus" width="20" height="14"> <img class="product" src="media/b3d-20x14.png" alt="Blitz3D" title="Blitz3D" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzBasic](BlitzBasic) · [Display](BlitzBasic-Display)

</div>


```blitzbasic
CountGfxModes:Int32
```

**Returns:** The number of modes.

## Description

The number of full screen display modes. Use [GfxModeWidth](GfxModeWidth), [GfxModeHeight](GfxModeHeight) and [GfxModeDepth](GfxModeDepth) with a number from 1 to this value to learn what each mode is.

## Differences

* The modes are the ones of the main display. When they cannot be asked, for example without a display, a list of common sizes is given: 19 sizes from 640x480 to 3840x2160 (640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1152x864, 1280x720, 1280x768, 1280x800, 1280x960, 1280x1024, 1360x768, 1366x768, 1440x900, 1600x900, 1600x1200, 1680x1050, 1920x1080, 1920x1200, 2560x1440 and 3840x2160), which is about what a display offers, so that a program that saved the number of a mode finds it again.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Print CountGfxModes() + " graphics modes"
For m = 1 To CountGfxModes()
	Print m + ": " + GfxModeWidth(m) + " x " + GfxModeHeight(m) + " x " + GfxModeDepth(m)
Next
WaitKey
```
